import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive insights
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
sensor_order = df.groupby('sensor_type')['price_usd'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', order=sensor_order, ax=ax1, palette='Set2')
ax1.set_title('Camera Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Megapixels over time
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
yearly_mp = df.groupby('model_year')['megapixels'].mean()
ax2.plot(yearly_mp.index, yearly_mp.values, marker='o', linewidth=2, markersize=4, color='#2E86AB')
ax2.set_title('Average Megapixels by Year', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 3. Price vs Megapixels scatter with body type
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
body_types = df['body_type'].unique()
colors = sns.color_palette('husl', n_colors=len(body_types))
for i, body in enumerate(body_types):
    data = df[df['body_type'] == body]
    ax3.scatter(data['megapixels'], data['price_usd'], alpha=0.6, 
               s=50, label=body, color=colors[i])
ax3.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Body Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax3.legend(title='Body Type', fontsize=9)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 4. 4K video capability distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
video_4k_counts = df['has_video_4k'].value_counts()
labels = ['No 4K', '4K']
colors_pie = ['#E63946', '#06D6A0']
ax4.pie(video_4k_counts.values, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
       colors=colors_pie, startangle=90)
ax4.set_title('4K Video Capability', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

# 5. Top brands by count
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, :2])
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10)
sns.barplot(x=top_brands.values, y=top_brands.index, ax=ax5, palette='viridis')
ax5.set_title('Top 10 Camera Brands by Model Count', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Number of Models', fontsize=11)
ax5.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)

# 6. Weight vs Price correlation
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
ax6.scatter(df['weight_grams'], df['price_usd'], alpha=0.5, s=30, color='#F77F00')
z = np.polyfit(df['weight_grams'], df['price_usd'], 1)
p = np.poly1d(z)
ax6.plot(df['weight_grams'].sort_values(), p(df['weight_grams'].sort_values()), 
        "r--", linewidth=2, alpha=0.8, label=f'Trend')
ax6.set_title('Weight vs Price', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=11)
ax6.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax6.legend(fontsize=9)
ax6.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
